text:
erin: quick note— customer hit duplicated side-effects in the quickstart when a 429 arrived exactly as our SDK refreshed tokens. small repro below.

noah: ouch. minimal repro?

erin: 1) run quickstart createItem until server returns 429. 2) during backoff force auth rotation. 3) SDK refresh finishes and retry immediately without idempotency key -> duplicate item created.

sam: quickstart intentionally tiny (no headers) but this is a real footgun. suggested minimal change: collapsed one-line idempotency example so the page stays small but safe.

erin: example (collapsed):
```js
const id = makeIdempotencyKey(userId, payload)
await client.createItem(payload, { headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': id } })
```

noah: SDK idea: detect token-version changes between attempts and mark retry as "refresh-triggered". policy options: `allow` (default), `require-idempotency`, `error`. if `require-idempotency` and no key present, surface an error instead of retrying. also emit telemetry `refresh_replay_attempted`.

sam: parity note: keep backoff defaults consistent across SDKs (base=100ms, cap=2s, factor=2, full-jitter). CI will add an e2e that simulates 429 + auth rotation.

ci-bot: CI plan: deterministic harness that pauses auth, returns 429, then resumes to reproduce race. will fail if duplicate side-effects occur.

erin: action items: @noah update quickstart (collapsed snippet), @sam draft SDK policy + telemetry, @ci-bot add e2e. target: next week. :thumbsup:
